verse.text: And so we know and rely on the love God has for us. God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.

reflection.scripture: And so we know and rely on the love God has for us. God is love. Whoever lives in love lives in God, and God in them.
reflection.observation: John writes with both certainty and invitation. He says we know and rely on God's love — not as a vague feeling, but as a settled reality we can depend on. Then he defines God himself: God is love. This isn't saying love is God, but that love is so central to God's nature that to live in love is to live in God. It's a two-way dwelling: we in God, God in us. The verse moves from head knowledge to heart reliance to embodied living.
reflection.application: Today, when I feel anxious, frustrated, or distant from God, I can return to this truth: God's love isn't conditional on my performance. I can actively rely on it — like leaning back into a chair I trust will hold me. One practical step: before reacting to someone today, pause and ask, 'Am I living in love right now?' If not, that's my cue to realign. Love isn't just a feeling; it's the atmosphere I'm meant to breathe.
reflection.prayer: Lord, thank You that Your love is not a theory — it's a reality I can build my life on. When I doubt, remind me that You are love itself. Help me live in that love today, not just receiving it but letting it flow through me to others. Let my words, my patience, and my presence reflect You. In Jesus' name, amen.
